title: Dangermond Preserve — Inferred Creek Water Surface Elevations (m5-v1, Jarrett steep-creek roughness)
snippet: m3-v2's channel and bed with a flow resistance that rises with slope on steep creeks, from Jarrett's (1984) field-fitted equation, which needs no grain size. Shown by default in the Creek Water Visualization.
description:
What this is
Inferred water surface elevation (WSE) and water depth for every short stretch of creek (Creek Segment) in the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, California, every hour from October 2020 to January 2023 and every month from 1950 to 2024, in meters above the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88). This is the version the Creek Water Visualization shows by default.

How it was made
Modeled stream flow (NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly; California Natural Flows, monthly) is shared out to each creek stretch by the land area draining into it. The creek bed is the 1-meter USGS 3DEP lidar at the creek's lowest point, with no smoothing. At one cross-section per stretch, a flow-resistance law fitted to steep mountain streams (Jarrett, 1984) gives the water depth; on steep creeks the water runs slower and deeper than with a fixed Manning roughness. Pools behind steps are filled level.

Accuracy and limits
These are estimates, not measurements. The stream flows are modeled without gauge correction and may be off by a factor of 2 to 5, so the timing of rises and falls is more reliable than the heights. The water depth assumes steady flow over a bare-earth lidar terrain that cannot see the underwater channel bed. Use them for research and visualization.

Service
https://dangermondpreserve-spatial.com/server/rest/services/Hosted/creek_water_visualization_modeled_wse_m5_v1/FeatureServer

Technical details

Dangermond Preserve — Inferred Creek Water Surface Elevations (m5-v1, Jarrett steep-creek roughness). Data-Product Version m5-v1 of m5-flowline-profile-jarrett-depth. Shared publicly as the Creek Water Visualization's default modeled water; other versions stay private.

How it is made: Modeled water-surface elevation (m NAVD88) and junction water depth per Creek Segment. Discharge per NHDPlusV2 reach (NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly; California Natural Flows, monthly) is scaled to each Creek Segment by the USGS drainage-area ratio method (segment Q = reach Q × drainageAreaRatio from the crosswalk (USGS drainage-area ratio method, ratio capped at 1), as m1). Flowline channel profile (Jarrett steep-creek depth), version 1: m3 v2’s channel, raw lidar bed, anchor cross-section, discharge and pool-filled water surface, with a steep-creek roughness: Jarrett (1984), n = 0.32 S^0.38 R^−0.16, which needs no grain size, blended from Manning’s n 0.04/0.07 over 2–8% slope as in m4. Time-varying values are stored as Held WSE Intervals: a new interval starts when the anchor WSE or either junction depth changes.

Change: new method: New method: m3 v2 with Jarrett’s (1984) flow resistance on slopes above 2% (full law from 8%), the same blend as m4.

WSE Anchor Point: channelRibbon.anchorLonLat (the anchor station's lowest point, WGS 84) of flowline-channel-ribbon v2, the WSE Polygon Generation Method version built on modeled WSE m3-v2, whose channel this version solves on; its anchorBedElevationM must equal the Time Series anchorBedElevationM. A Creek Segment without a ribbon has no anchor point (null). Anchor depth = wse_m − anchor_bed_elevation_m.

Held WSE Interval tables: One row per Creek Segment and stretch of time in which wse_m (m NAVD88) and both junction water depths stay constant; valid_from_utc inclusive, valid_until_utc exclusive, so every hourly or monthly value can be rebuilt exactly. Junction WSE = the junction bed column of the Creek Segments layer + the junction depth.

Raw hourly values: Every hourly value of every Creek Segment, one zipped CSV item per water year in the same portal folder (columns segment_id, tnc_comid, time_utc, wse_m, junction_depth_upstream_m, junction_depth_downstream_m).

Null values: null_values_note is the Stage 3 warning for a Creek Segment whose values are all null (no discharge beyond the Drainage-Area Ratio Transfer distance, or a segment lying wholly on a breached road or railroad fill); null otherwise. Such a segment's wse_m and junction depths stay null in every table.

Channel: Solved on the channel of modeled WSE m3-v2; draw it with that version's channel-ribbon polygons.

Published from the creek-water-visualization repository (UCS-285, UCS-298).
